validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed, high tier, 3 independent origins that all NAME 'Saginaw Trail Pipeline' explicitly: (1) Consumers Energy's own Nov 23 2020 PR Newswire completion release, (2) Offshore-Technology/GlobalData's project database (this URL is still served at the legacy 'hydrocarbons-technology.com' host but the site has been rebranded/merged into offshore-technology.com; content intact, dated Apr 25 2019), and (3) Farm Progress's Jan 12 2017 trade-press coverage of the MPSC siting filing. This is real, built infrastructure, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a natural-gas transmission pipeline (24-in replacement/upgrade of Consumers Energy's 1940s-vintage Line 2800, built under the company's Transmission Enhancements for Deliverability-Integrity (TED-I) program). It is an INTRASTATE Michigan utility project regulated by the Michigan Public Service Commission (Consumers Energy filed for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, Sept 2 2016; MPSC approved May 2017) -- FERC silence is expected here and is not an existence concern (SOP point b). DUPLICATE: checked the full 46-row roster; no other row plausibly matches this Saginaw County-to-Oakland County, Michigan intrastate line -- not a relabel of any Rover/Vector/NEXUS row (those are interstate Ohio->Michigan lines on a different corridor and under different jurisdiction/owner). No duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: StartState/Province=Michigan and EndState/Province=Michigan both confirmed directly (hydrocarbons-technology: 'runs from Saginaw County to Oakland County via Genesee County, Michigan'; PR Newswire names Shiawassee NWR in Saginaw County and Kensington Metropark in Oakland County as work sites along the route). Owner1=CMS Energy (100%) is correct as the ultimate parent holding company -- PR Newswire states explicitly 'Consumers Energy ... is the principal subsidiary of CMS Energy (NYSE: CMS)', independently corroborated by Wikipedia's CMS Energy infobox (subsidiaries: Consumers Energy), itself sourced to CMS Energy's SEC 10-K. Consumers Energy is the actual builder/operator per every source, which is what I staged into the (previously blank) Operator field. SPEC: Diameter=24in CONFIRMED by 2 independent sources -- hydrocarbons-technology ('Saginaw Trail will be a 24in-diameter pipeline') AND Farm Progress ('upgrade to 24-inch-diameter pipe from 12- to 16-inch diameter'), high tier. Length=94.00mi CONFIRMED by 2 independent sources -- Farm Progress states the exact figure ('The Saginaw Trail Pipeline, if approved as proposed, will span 94 miles') and hydrocarbons-technology's '152km-long pipeline' converts to 94.4mi, high tier. Note: PR Newswire's headline/body describes 'about 90 miles' and 'about 90 miles of new, larger pipeline' -- I checked this against the other two sources rather than accepting it uncritically; it is a rounded, less-precise figure in a press release (the release itself describes total replaced-plus-rerouted mileage informally), not a genuine disagreement with the two sources that independently converge on 94/94.4 miles, so I did not file it as a spec concern. SegmentCost=$610,000,000 USD CONFIRMED EXACTLY by 2 independent sources -- PR Newswire ('a four-year, $610 million construction project') and hydrocarbons-technology ('Investment $610m'), high tier. Opened and read to exhaustion: the PR Newswire release, the hydrocarbons-technology/offshore-technology project profile, and the Farm Progress article (all 4 of the row's 8 harvested wiki citations that could plausibly name this specific pipeline; the EIA data-portal homepage and the S&P Global blog post are generic aggregate citations shared across many rows in this batch's harvested pool and FAIL url_verifier's name check -- consistent with the sweep's calibration note that a generic-only citation is itself a flag, except here two better, pipeline-naming sources already exist so it is not an existence concern). The consumersenergy.com URL cited on the wiki page (cite_note-source2-6) now 200s but silently redirects to a generic 'Natural Gas Operations' landing page that never says 'Saginaw Trail' -- the project-specific page has been retired/folded into a general page; per the blocked-fetch/dead-link rule this is not a confirmed 404 so I am not asserting it is gone, but it can no longer be cited (fails the naming test) and should not be proposed as a ref. ANCILLARY (out of my worklist scope, but worth flagging): the live sheet's StartLocation and EndLocation cells are BOTH blank (not just missing refs) even though State/Prefecture/Country are filled -- hydrocarbons-technology names the exact termini ('from Tittabawassee Township in Saginaw County to south of Milford in Oakland County'), which I staged as a fill under the Location [ref] cluster since that unit was in my worklist. PipelineType is ALSO blank on the live sheet (should be 'transmission') but no 'PipelineType [ref]' unit appeared in my assigned worklist slice for this row, so I have not staged a fill for it -- flagging it here for the orchestrator/next pass since it is an easy, well-sourced fill (all 3 sources describe a natural gas transmission pipeline).
